# QFT exclusion from the current goal

The [direct-user scope record](authorization.json) transcribes the maintainer's
explicit exclusion of QFT implementation completion from 0.3.0-alpha and the
current goal. The [later clarification](clarification-02.json) explicitly extends
this exclusion to v0.3.0 and requires trial retention only under experimental/.
No future target or completion credit is selected.
GitHub remains the decisions/progress ledger: [#317](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/issues/317),
[#142](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/issues/142),
[#32](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/issues/32) and
[#152](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/issues/152) now carry the scope override.

Before/after Issue snapshots retain all historical text and checkboxes. #317
has 21 applicable criteria (original20 plus final general family-naming rule);
its three QFT-specific additions are explicitly excluded, not completed. The
selected denominator remains111 and confirmed completion14 (12.61%). An
independent [ordinary review](review.json) checked the exact criterion counts
and repaired one overbroad historical-preservation sentence before publication.

No active release requirements/acceptance snapshot exists. The future caller-
reviewed requirements must bind only applicable criteria and this explicit
scope decision. No gate schema, proof status, protected text or adopted
interpretation changed. Existing fixed-QFT functionality and historical
evidence remain; active namespace consumers may undergo ordinary migration
while preserving contracts, phase, interfaces and notices.

The [experimental attempts](../../../../experimental/qft/README.md) retain the
exact source bytes. The original family/exact-request sessions and associated
trial tooling are preserved in checked history archives there; their old fixture
directories were removed. Historical member paths/hashes are unchanged, and the
two archived sessions leave the dynamic authoring-checker count. No historical
command is replayed; this is not an active QFT development task or release gate.

Documentation and source-edition checks validate these scope/retention edits.
The existing31 readiness regressions pass; they do not create a complete
acceptance index or establish release readiness. The separate common-checker
packet records its actual Rust and97 policy regressions.
